errorBoundary.title: Oops, something went wrong
errorBoundary.text: The interface hit an unexpected error. Your chats and data are safely stored. Reload the page to continue.

install.title: Install as app
install.text: KI Kobold can be installed as an app - it then opens in its own window without a browser bar and can be started offline.

welcome.title: Hello & welcome!
welcome.subtitle: KI Kobold - your AI chat, running entirely in your browser.
welcome.localText: All messages and responses are generated directly in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server - your data never leaves your device.
welcome.modelText: For the AI to work, you need to download a model first. The download comes directly from this website, is cached in your browser and is instantly ready the next time.
welcome.chatText: Pick a model at the top, type your message and send it - done. No account, no sign-up.
welcome.downloadHint: Tip: During the first model download you will see a progress bar with size, speed and remaining time.

tour.step1Text: Here you pick your AI model. The first time it is downloaded - with a progress bar. After that it is stored in your browser and ready instantly. Some models think visibly - which ones those are and where each model shines is explained under Menu → Models.
tour.step2Text: Profiles change the style of the answers: 'Precise' for facts, 'Creative' for ideas.
tour.step3Text: 'Export Chat' saves the current chat as a file, 'Share' copies it to your clipboard. Full backup and import live under menu → Data.
tour.step4Text: Here you can find older messages in the current chat.
tour.step5Text: Type your message and send it. Use the microphone to dictate, the paperclip to attach files.
tour.step6Text: Here you find new chats, the history, profiles, the memory, the library, the models page with strengths and weaknesses of every model, data & backup, settings, help, the roadmap, the AI lexicon and contact.

data.title: Data & Backup
data.introText: All your data lives entirely in your browser: chats, memory, library and downloaded models. Here you see what is stored, create a complete backup, restore it or delete everything.
data.backupText: The backup contains all chats, the memory and the library as one JSON file - perfect for safekeeping or moving to another device. On import, chats with the same ID are overwritten; memory and library are merged in.
data.dangerText: Permanently deletes all chats, memory entries and library files from your browser. Downloaded models stay (you can delete those in the settings). Create a backup first if you care about the data!
data.deleteAllConfirm: Really delete ALL chats, memory entries and library files? This cannot be undone.
data.deleteAllConfirm2: Are you sure? Without a backup the data is gone afterwards.
data.clearCacheText: The app's browser cache stores files for a fast start. Models and chats are untouched by the cleanup - cached files reload on next use.
data.clearCacheDone: Cleanup started - older cache entries are being deleted.

library.title: Library
library.introText: Store files you need again and again - notes, code snippets or tables. In the chat you reference a file with @Name and the AI receives its content as context.
library.addHint: Allowed are text files (.txt, .md, .csv, .json, code files, ...) up to 512 KB. PDF, Word and images do not belong in the library - the AI only understands text.
library.errorType: "{{name}}" is not supported - only text files up to 512 KB are allowed.
library.errorEmpty: The file is empty or contains no readable text.
library.empty: No files in the library yet. Add a text file above to reference it in the chat.
library.howToTitle: How to use the library in the chat
library.howToText: Simply write @ followed by the file name in your message - for example "Summarize @notes". You can leave out the extension (@notes instead of @notes.txt). At most 4000 characters per file flow into a request, 12000 in total - so trim large files to the essentials.

attachments.dropWarningText: Files cannot be dropped here. Use the paperclip (📎) next to the input field to attach a file instead.

contact.title: Contact
contact.introText: Do you have questions about KI Kobold or need help? Just get in touch - send an email to the address below and we will get back to you.
contact.beforeWritingText: You can already find many answers on the help page: how the models work, what they can and cannot do, how to use import/export and the memory. If that does not help, we look forward to your message. Describe your issue as precisely as possible - which browser you use, which model and what you did.

browserWarning.firefoxTitle: Firefox detected: the AI runs slower here
browserWarning.firefoxText: The AI models work noticeably slower in Firefox than in Chrome or Edge - answers often appear word by word. Please use Chrome or Edge for full speed.
browserWarning.firefoxReason: Reason: Firefox does not support JSPI (JavaScript Promise Integration). Because of that, the engine has to take a slow detour for WASM models like LFM 2.5. This is a browser limitation and cannot be fixed from this website.

whatsNew.title: What's new
whatsNew.subtitle: A few things have changed since your last visit:

v420.item1: Menu cleaned up: Management (profiles, memory, library, models, data) and "Help & Legal" are now collapsible groups - the sidebar shows the essentials.
v420.item2: Chat history takes the spotlight: it is now always visible (no longer only on the chat tab) and gets all the space below the menu.
v420.item3: Folders for chats: the history supports folders - create, rename, move chats via 📁, collapse folders. Deleting a folder keeps the chats.
v420.item4: Backup format v1.3: folders are included in export/import.

v410.item1: Text size is now adjustable directly in the chat: the Aa button next to the search offers all four levels - no detour to the settings.
v410.item2: High contrast: new toggle (Settings → Accessibility) boosts text and border contrast; the system "more contrast" preference is respected automatically.
v410.item3: Readable font: Atkinson Hyperlegible - designed for low vision, self-hosted (no Google server involved).
v410.item4: Navigate messages by keyboard: J/K jumps between messages (with a visible focus), C copies the focused message, ? shows all shortcuts right in the chat.
v410.item5: Read-aloud button per message: every message can be read aloud and stopped individually - with an adjustable speech rate.
v410.item6: Touch optimization: small buttons get invisibly enlarged hit areas on touch devices (44px, without changing their look).
v410.item7: Under the hood: switching the language now sets the lang attribute (screen readers pronounce English correctly), profile cards and image previews are keyboard-operable, and an a11y linter guards against new issues in CI.

v400.item1: Adjustable text size: small to very large - scales the entire interface (Settings → Accessibility).
v400.item2: Increased readability: more line height and slight letter spacing in messages and the input field.
v400.item3: Reduce animations: movement and transitions can be disabled - independent of the system setting.
v400.item4: Screen reader support: skip link to the chat, announcements when the AI starts and finishes answering, clear "You"/"AI" labels on messages.
v400.item5: Keyboard: visible focus rings everywhere, dialogs trap the Tab focus (Esc closes), the chat list is now operable by keyboard.
v400.item6: Improved contrast: text in light and dark mode now meets WCAG - including darker user bubbles and more readable hint texts.
v400.item7: Minimum font sizes: tiny 11-pixel texts raised to 12 pixels, touch buttons at least 24 pixels.
v400.item8: Model downloads are announced to screen readers - start and phase, without flooding percentages.

v340.item1: Crash protection: when an unexpected error occurs, the interface stays visible instead of turning white - your data is safe, one click reloads.
v340.item2: Keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+K (or Cmd+K) opens and closes the chat search, Esc cancels the running generation.
v340.item3: The browser tab title now shows what is currently happening - handy with multiple tabs.
v340.item4: The chat search now highlights matches in your own messages too.
v340.item5: New subtle hint to install the site as an app (where the browser supports it).
v340.item6: Error messages while loading a model are now bilingual (German/English).
v340.item7: New AI lexicon (Menu → Lexicon): simply explains what AI, machine learning and language models are, what 'thinking' means, which models exist - and what AI can and cannot do. With glossary.
v340.item8: Thinking mode can be turned off: on thinking models (Qwen) the 💭 button toggles reasoning on and off - off means faster answers for simple questions.
v340.item9: Faster start: the AI engine (the largest part of the app) only loads when a model is actually needed - math formatting likewise only on demand. Long chats stay smooth: older messages load when you scroll up.

v330.item1: New models: Qwen 3.5 2B, Qwen 3 1.7B and Qwen 3 0.6B replace Gemma 2 and Qwen 2. All three think visibly - the reasoning appears collapsible in the answer.
v330.item2: New models page (Menu → Models): strengths and weaknesses of every model, release date, download size and engine at a glance.
v330.item3: New roadmap (Menu → Roadmap): planned improvements - explicitly without any timeline.
v330.item4: Cleaned up: The old models (Gemma 2 2B, Qwen 2 0.5B) are gone - from the server as well. If you still had them downloaded, your browser storage is freed automatically on the next start.
v330.item5: Mentions: Typing @ in the chat suggests your library files - filtered as you type and selectable with arrow keys. The new 📚 button in the chat field opens the list directly.

v321.item1: Context error fixed: attachments and long conversations no longer exceed the model window - context raised from 1024 to 4096 tokens, large attachments are trimmed.
v321.item2: Download speed: Gemma 2 and Qwen now show size, speed and remaining time again.

v320.item1: Data & backup: new menu item with an overview of everything stored locally, plus full backup export and import.
v320.item2: Delete everything: clears chats, memory and library with one click (with a double confirmation).

v310.item1: Bugfix: the chat no longer shows "Loading model" when nothing is loading at all.
v310.item2: What's-new dialog: now scrolls cleanly, the close button always stays visible.
v310.item3: Returning users now reliably see what changed after an update.

v300.item1: Library: store files once and use them in the chat via @Name (menu → Library).
v300.item2: Memory with ready-made fields: fill in name, work, hobbies and location directly.
v300.item3: New settings: theme (system/light/dark), default profile and model, read-aloud on/off, memory on/off.
v300.item4: PWA: the page can be installed as an app - on smartphone and desktop.
v300.item5: Attachments: the help now explains exactly which files work - and dragging a file shows a warning.

v240.item1: What's-new display: when something changes, you see a short summary on your next visit.
v240.item2: Help page: the introduction can now be restarted at any time, and all past changes are listed there.

v230.item1: Contact page: if you have questions or need help, you can now reach out via email (menu → Contact).
v230.item2: Firefox warning: Firefox users see a notice explaining why the AI is slower there.

v220.item1: Memory: store facts about yourself (name, job, preferences) that the AI knows in every chat (menu → Memory).
v220.item2: Export/import now backs up the memory and restores it on import.

v210.item1: Welcome page and guided introduction on your first visit.
v210.item2: Download progress with size, speed and estimated time remaining.

v200.item1: New design, curated models (LFM 2.5, Gemma 2, Qwen 2) - models are downloaded directly from this website.

memory.introText: Write down facts about yourself that the AI should know with every message. The entries apply to all chats and are included in exports as a backup. The AI reads the memory but does not store anything itself: it does not automatically remember what you tell it.
memory.fieldsHint: Saved automatically when you leave the field. Emptying it deletes the entry.
memory.placeholder: e.g. I am Max and I live in Exampletown.

help.title: Help
help.introText: KI Kobold is a place to try out artificial intelligence - directly in your browser. No sign-up, no account, free. Pick a model, download it once and get started. All messages and answers stay on your device.
help.gettingStartedText: Pick a model at the top of the chat and confirm the one-time download - you will see size, speed and estimated time remaining. After that the model is stored in your browser and ready instantly. Then simply type your message and send it.
help.modelsTitle: The Models - What They Can and Cannot Do
help.modelsCan1: Answer general questions, write, summarize and translate texts
help.modelsCan2: Explain simple programming tasks and write small code examples
help.modelsCan3: Collect ideas, brainstorm and write creatively
help.modelsCannot1: No internet access: no current news, stock prices or weather data
help.modelsCannot2: Limited knowledge - small models make mistakes and sometimes invent facts. Always verify important information!
help.modelsCannot3: No image or file analysis - the AI only understands text
help.modelsCannot4: No memory beyond the chat - the AI does not remember anything on its own. The 'Memory' feature helps (see below)
help.modelsHint: LFM 2.5 runs in every browser (including Firefox) but is noticeably slower there. Gemma 2 and Qwen 2 need Chrome or Edge and are very fast there.
help.contextTitle: How the AI Understands Your Chat
help.contextText: With every message, the AI receives the last 10 messages of the current chat as history - older messages are not included. In very long chats the AI 'forgets' the beginning. Start a new chat for a fresh start. Imported chats are treated the same way: there too, the AI knows the last 10 messages.
help.profilesDescription: Profiles control how the AI behaves: the system prompt defines its personality (for example 'Answer briefly and precisely'), the temperature determines how creative or factual the answers are. You can switch the active profile at the top of the chat; it applies to all messages you send afterwards.
help.memoryTitle: Memory - What the AI Knows About You
help.memoryText: Normally the AI only knows the current chat (see above). Under 'Memory' in the menu you can store facts about yourself which are then included with every message in every chat - with ready-made fields for name, work, hobbies and location plus your own free entries. The AI reads these entries but does not store anything itself: what you tell it in a chat is not remembered automatically. You can edit or delete entries at any time. The memory is limited (1000 characters in total) so the small models are not overwhelmed.
help.memoryHowTo: Example entries: 'I am Max', 'I work as a baker', 'I like hiking and gaming'.
help.importExportIntro: Your chats belong to you - back them up, move them to another device or restore them at any time:
help.importExportList1: 'Export Chat' saves the current chat as a JSON file
help.importExportList2: 'Share' copies the current chat as readable text to your clipboard
help.importExportList3: Menu → Data: create a complete backup of all chats, the memory and the library
help.importExportList4: Menu → Data: import a backup (on another device or browser as well) or delete all data
help.importExportHint: On import, chats with the same ID are overwritten - no duplicates are created. Export files contain your memory and your library and restore both on import. Important: everything lives in your browser's database - clearing browser data deletes it all. Export a backup regularly (menu → Data) if your chats matter to you.
help.attachmentsIntro: You can give files to the AI - but only what it can actually process. The AI understands text only.
help.attachCan1: Text files as attachments: .txt, .md, .csv, .json, code files (.py, .js, .ts, ...) and more - up to 512 KB per file, at most 3 per message (via the paperclip 📎)
help.attachCan2: Images (PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF up to 4 MB) - but only with a multimodal model like LFM 2.5 that understands images
help.attachCan3: Library: store a file once and reuse it in any message via @Name (see below)
help.attachCannot1: PDF, Word, Excel and similar - the AI cannot read these formats. Copy the text into a .txt file and it works
help.attachCannot2: Drag & drop: files cannot be dropped into the window - a warning appears. Always use the paperclip 📎
help.attachCannot3: Images with models without image support - the attachment is then ignored
help.attachDropHint: Important: if you drag a file into the window, the page shows a warning that drag & drop is not supported. The file is not opened and not sent.
help.libraryText: Instead of attaching the same file over and over, store it once under menu → Library. In the chat you then write @Name in your message (e.g. "What do @notes say?") and the AI receives the file content as context. The same text formats as for attachments are allowed (up to 512 KB); PDF, Word and images do not work. At most 4000 characters per file flow into a request.
help.libraryHint: Example: store notes.txt in the library, then ask: "Summarize @notes in three points."
help.privacyText: Everything runs locally in your browser: models are downloaded from this website and stored in the browser, messages are never sent to any server. No accounts, no tracking, no cloud.
help.tip1: Ask clear, specific questions - small models need unambiguous instructions
help.tip2: Break complex tasks into several small messages
help.tip3: Try different profiles: 'Precise' for facts, 'Creative' for ideas
help.tip4: If an answer is nonsense: rephrase the question or start a new chat
help.shortcutsIntro: These shortcuts save you trips to the mouse:
help.shortcutSearch: Ctrl+K / Cmd+K: open and close the chat search
help.shortcutCancel: Esc: cancel the running generation (and close open popups)
help.contactSupport: The best way is to simply try everything out - that's exactly what this page is for. If you have questions or need help, reach out via the contact page (menu → Contact).
help.tourWhatsNewText: Did you skip the introduction or want to see it again? Here you can restart it at any time. You can also review all changes from the last versions.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.intro: Here you can see which improvements and features are planned for KI Kobold. The list shows the direction we want to take - for trying things out, having your say and looking forward.
roadmap.noTimeline: Important: This roadmap has no chronological order. There are no dates, no sequence and no promises - these are ideas we want to work on. Some may arrive soon, some later, and the list can change at any time.
roadmap.stability2: Stuck downloads should be able to abort and restart instead of waiting forever.
roadmap.downloads2: Interrupted model downloads should be resumable instead of starting over from scratch.
roadmap.downloads3: Show which engine (WebGPU or the fallback) is currently active.
roadmap.downloads4: A model that can generate images is being explored: possible in the browser in principle, but the downloads would be very large and generation slow - under reserve.
roadmap.storage1: A storage overview: what models, chats and caches are using - with cleanup buttons.
roadmap.storage3: An improved offline indicator so the status is always visible.

wiki.title: AI Lexicon
wiki.subtitle: Explained simply: what AI is, how it works - and what it can and cannot do. This page needs no model: everything here is fixed text.
wiki.aiText: AI is an umbrella term for computer programs that solve tasks which normally need human thinking: understanding and writing text, describing images, translating languages or answering questions. Important: today's AI has no consciousness and no feelings - it is a very powerful form of pattern recognition.
wiki.aiPoint1: Everyday examples: spam filters, voice assistants, translators, face recognition on your phone.
wiki.aiPoint2: 'Intelligent' does not mean 'conscious': AI recognizes patterns in data - it does not understand like a human.
wiki.aiPoint3: On this site the AI runs entirely in your browser - no server, no cloud.
wiki.mlText: In the past, computers were programmed with rules ('if X, then Y'). Machine learning turns this around: the computer gets very many examples and finds the patterns in them itself. A spam filter learns from millions of real emails what spam is - without anyone writing a single rule.
wiki.mlPoint1: Training = learning: the model adjusts its internal numbers until it can 'predict' the examples well.
wiki.mlPoint2: More good examples make a better model - but it does not know anything that was not in the examples.
wiki.llmText: A Large Language Model (LLM) is at its core a very good word-prediction machine: for any text it computes which word most likely comes next. Word by word, whole answers emerge this way. Sounds simple - but it is the foundation of ChatGPT and the models on this site.
wiki.llmPoint1: Token: models do not work with words but with text pieces (tokens) - roughly 3-4 characters in English.
wiki.llmPoint2: Context window: how much text the model can 'keep in mind' at once (here e.g. 8,000 to 262,000 tokens). Anything beyond that is dropped.
wiki.llmPoint3: Parameters: the model's 'memory cells'. More parameters = usually better answers, but larger downloads.
wiki.thinkingText: Some models 'think out loud' before answering: they break the task into steps, try approaches and correct themselves. Only afterwards do they write the actual answer. On this site the Qwen models show this reasoning as a collapsible section - you can watch the AI think.
wiki.thinkingUseful3: Planning: 'first an outline, then the text'
wiki.thinkingNot1: Simple questions ('How many hours are in a day?')
wiki.thinkingHint: Tip: under Menu → Models you can see which models here think along.
wiki.modelsIntro: A short map of well-known AI models. The last two run directly here on this site - marked with 🏠.
wiki.modelGptText: The best-known AI chat (launched 2022). Runs only in the cloud - needs internet and an account.
wiki.modelGeminiText: Google's AI, connected to Search and Android. Also cloud-based.
wiki.modelClaudeText: Considered especially strong with long texts. Cloud-based.
wiki.modelLlamaText: Open model family from Meta - anyone may download and run it themselves. The foundation of many local AI applications.
wiki.modelMistralText: European open models, known for a lot of performance in a small size.
wiki.modelQwenText: Open model family from China. The Qwen 3 models on this site come from it - they think visibly and compute locally in your browser.
wiki.modelLfmText: Young, very efficient model family. The LFM model here runs in almost any browser, even without WebGPU.
wiki.modelsLocalNote: The difference: cloud models send your texts to foreign servers. The models here compute on your device - your messages never leave it.
wiki.canTitle: What AI can do - and what it cannot
wiki.can1: Writing, summarizing, rephrasing and translating texts
wiki.can2: Explaining things - from 'What is DNA?' to 'How does a contract work?'
wiki.can5: Extracting the essentials from long texts (including your library files)
wiki.cannot1: Guarantee the truth - models sometimes invent convincingly sounding facts ('hallucinations')
wiki.cannot2: Know what is happening in the world today - its knowledge ends with training
wiki.cannot3: Calculate reliably like a calculator - better double-check numbers
wiki.cannot4: Remember beyond the chat - it only knows what is in the chat and the memory
wiki.cannot5: Have real feelings or consciousness - it only imitates understanding very convincingly
wiki.hallucinationText: When a model does not know an answer, it does not always say so - it simply types the most probable next word. This can produce false but very believable answers: invented book titles, wrong numbers, sources that do not exist. Therefore: always double-check important statements - especially with the small local models on this site.
wiki.termTokenDef: Text piece that models compute with - roughly 3-4 characters. The model reads and writes tokens, not letters.
wiki.termContextDef: The model's 'working memory': everything that fits in at once (system prompt, memory, history, your message). When it is full, the oldest parts are dropped.
wiki.termParametersDef: The internal numbers of a model, created during training. '1.7B' = 1.7 billion parameters. More parameters = usually smarter, but larger downloads.
wiki.termQuantizationDef: Compression of the model: numbers are stored more coarsely so it fits into the browser. 'Q4' means 4 bits per number - smaller and faster, minimally less precise.
wiki.termTemperatureDef: The creativity dial (0 to 2): low = sober and predictable, high = surprising ideas. Adjustable in the profiles.
wiki.termHallucinationDef: When a model invents something it does not know - sounds convincing, but is wrong.
wiki.termWebgpuDef: Interface that lets websites use the graphics card - this is how the AI here computes fast. Needs Chrome or Edge.
wiki.termWasmDef: WebAssembly: allows fast programs in the browser, even without a graphics card. Runs almost everywhere, but slower.
wiki.termLocalDef: The model is downloaded once and then computes entirely on your device - without internet, your data never leaves the device.

modelsPage.title: Models
modelsPage.intro: Here you find all models available in KI Kobold. Every model runs entirely locally in your browser - it is downloaded once and then works even without an internet connection. The models differ in size, speed and capability.
modelsPage.thinkingHint: Models marked with 💭 think visibly: their reasoning appears in the answer as a collapsible section - collapsed by default.

qwen35.name: Qwen 3.5 2B
qwen35.s1: Best overall quality of all models - longer texts, better explanations
qwen35.s4: Huge context (262,144 characters) for extended conversations
qwen35.w1: Largest download of the WebGPU models (about 1 GB)
qwen35.w3: Thinking costs extra time and compute
qwen35.summary: The model for demanding tasks: writing, explaining and long conversations. If your device has WebGPU, start here.

qwen17.name: Qwen 3 1.7B
qwen17.s1: Specialist for math, logic and step-by-step tasks
qwen17.s3: Good ratio of size to reasoning quality
qwen17.summary: The thinker: on math problems and logic puzzles the model shows its reasoning - collapsible right in the answer.

qwen06.name: Qwen 3 0.6B
qwen06.s1: Smallest download (335 MB) and fastest answers
qwen06.w2: Thinking is weak at this size
qwen06.w3: Not suited for long texts and complex topics
qwen06.summary: For trying things out and short questions: fastest to download and fastest to answer - fully sufficient for simple tasks.

lfm.name: LFM 2.5 1.6B
lfm.s1: Runs in any browser - even without WebGPU, in Firefox and Safari
lfm.s3: Balanced quality for everyday tasks, knowledge and texts
lfm.s4: Automatic fallback when WebGPU is missing
lfm.w1: Less knowledge than the larger models
lfm.summary: The all-rounder for every browser: the only model that runs without WebGPU - and the only one with image understanding.

settings.title: Settings
settings.defaultsText: Defines which profile and model the page starts with.
settings.defaultModelHint: Only applied if the model is already downloaded - otherwise you pick it in the chat as usual.
settings.autoSpeakHint: Answers are read aloud automatically with text-to-speech after they arrive.
settings.memoryEnabledHint: Memory entries are included with every message. Without this checkbox the AI ignores your memory.
settings.a11yText: Adjust text size, readability and animations to your needs.
settings.textSizeHint: Scales the whole interface - useful for smaller or larger text.
settings.readableTextHint: More line height and slight letter spacing in messages and the input field.
settings.reduceMotionHint: Hides movement and transitions - independent of the system setting.
settings.readableFontHint: A typeface specifically designed for low vision - letter shapes that are hard to confuse.
settings.highContrastHint: Boosts text and border contrast in light and dark mode beyond WCAG AA.
settings.speechRateHint: Speed of the text-to-speech output - applies to auto-speak and the per-message read-aloud button.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.subtitle: Last updated: October 2026
privacy.controllerText: The controller for data processing on this website is Roman Thiel, operator of kikobold.net (see address below).
privacy.localTitle: How KI Kobold works - everything stays on your device
privacy.localText1: KI Kobold processes your chat messages exclusively locally in your browser. The AI models are downloaded to your device and the answers are computed there - none of your messages are sent to or processed on a server.
privacy.localText2: Your chats are stored in your browser's IndexedDB, settings and profiles in localStorage. This data never leaves your device. You can back it up at any time via the export/import function or delete it on the data page.
privacy.logsText1: When you visit the website, the hosting provider (Hetzner Online GmbH, Germany) records technically necessary server log data: your IP address, the time of access, the requested file, the amount of data transferred and the browser identifier. This data is technically required to serve the website and ensure its security.
privacy.logsText2: The legal basis is Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR (legitimate interest in a secure and stable operation). The log data is routinely deleted after a short period; it is not merged with other data sources.
privacy.modelsText1: The AI models are primarily downloaded from this website's own webspace (Germany). Only if it is unreachable, a fallback to the public HuggingFace CDN (Hugging Face Inc., USA) kicks in automatically. The provider then sees your IP address and the requested file.
privacy.modelsText2: The legal basis is likewise Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR. For the fallback, the EU Commission's standard contractual clauses apply as safeguards for the data transfer to the USA. The download only starts after your confirmation.
privacy.trackingText1: This website does not set cookies, uses no analytics, no advertising and no social media plugins. There is no telemetry and no user accounts.
privacy.trackingText2: The local storage (IndexedDB, localStorage) serves exclusively to operate the app (chats, settings, downloaded models) and is technically necessary - it lives in your browser and is not visible to us.
privacy.rightsText1: You have the right of access (Art. 15 GDPR), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18), data portability (Art. 20) and the right to object to processing (Art. 21). Since almost all data is stored locally on your device, you can delete it yourself via the app's data page.
privacy.rightsText2: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR). Please direct privacy requests to the email address below.

imprint.title: Imprint
imprint.subtitle: Information pursuant to § 5 DDG (German Digital Services Act)
imprint.vatText: No VAT identification number - kikobold.net is a private, non-commercial project.
imprint.contentTitle: Liability for content and AI answers
imprint.contentText: The content of this website is created with the greatest care. However, the AI models' answers are generated locally on your device and may be incorrect or incomplete (so-called hallucinations). No liability is assumed for the accuracy, completeness or timeliness of AI answers - please always verify important information against independent sources.
imprint.linksText: This website contains links to external third-party websites (e.g. model providers such as HuggingFace). We have no influence on their content and therefore cannot guarantee it. No legal violations were apparent at the time of linking.
imprint.copyrightText: The app is currently not published publicly on Git - the source code is kept in a private repository. Publication under the MIT license is planned. The integrated AI models are subject to the licenses of their respective providers (LiquidAI, Qwen/Alibaba) and are served unmodified from public sources.
